title_chain.zh_h1: 塞缪尔·亚历山大 Alexander, Samuel (Emily A. E. Thomas)

spot.html_text: Alexander’s writing on art falls into two kinds. First, there are essays on literature and art. These are all reprinted in Alexander’s (1939), and cover a wide range of topics: from the art of Jane Austen, to the writings of Pascal, to the origin of the creative impulse. Second, there are the pieces comprising Alexander’s account of value. Alexander’s early interest in ethics—exemplified in his first monograph (1889)—survived in his later work as a preoccupation with the nature of value, albeit
